content.content: deccy validate exercises the validity, resolution, coverage, topology, and content custody checks and reports failures to the caller; it changes nothing and records no verdicts.
content.rationale: Checks must be invokable without becoming state, so one verb exposes all of them: validity, resolution and coverage keep a node answerable to the graph's own structure; starting with D9 the topology check joins them, because a graph whose edges run against history is still structurally well-formed; and content custody joins the same set one layer lower, so the sentence that lists the checks gains a fifth name rather than the verb gaining a second check. The set is the one the prerequisite orwrynyn decides, and a surface that named four of its five checks would be an incomplete surface rather than a narrower one: naming the fifth is what keeps this decision answerable to that set. Naming is all this node does with it. Neither the topology check nor the custody check is spelled out here — their rules are taken as given from the prerequisite orwrynyn — because a second copy of a rule inside this node would be free to drift from the first, and what each check reads, and what becomes of what it finds, are not re-settled on this surface. Reporting failures while changing nothing and recording no verdicts keeps the verb re-runnable and verdict-free at every invocation.
